name: Gombe
summary_text: Gombe applies Sharia criminal law as part of the twelve-state northern bloc adopted by 2002. The Sharia layer criminalises conduct beyond the federal SSMPA, including same-sex acts between women; the framework applies to Muslims, and its practical reach over visitors is mediated by arrest practice - including hisbah morality policing in the northern block - rather than by any formal 'tourists excepted' rule. No trans-specific incident or documented Hisbah activity appears in this dossier for Gombe. Reporting-decay caveats apply: absence of records reflects fear of outing and surveillance gaps, not absence of risk. Score 0.024 below the national 0.08. Tied with the generic-Sharia tier (Borno, Jigawa, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger): the enacted parallel criminal system is the deviation, without additional case-level or enforcement evidence to push further. Well above Kano (0.03) and Bauchi (0.02), which have death-penalty text or carried-out capital sentences respectively.

sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report (2004) on the extension of Sharia to criminal law in Nigeria: Zamfara's governor was first, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999 (in force 27 January 2000), and by 2002 twelve northern states had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation - to date the only states where Sharia courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases.

UK Home Office country-of-origin information note (June 2025) on sexual orientation and gender identity in Nigeria: Islamic law applies to Muslims in the 12 northern states and criminalises same-sex sexual acts both between men and between women; the maximum penalty for 'sodomy' for men is death in all 12 states and penalties for 'lesbianism' range from death to flogging and imprisonment; includes a dedicated section on enforcement of Sharia provisions and the attitude of the hisbah (morality police).
